subjects.displayTitle: Divine mediation: knowing through a living mirror
subjects.introduction: A watch cannot understand its maker, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá once told a questioner, and the human mind cannot grasp the Essence of God; left to itself it builds a conception that may be false, and the one test of it is whether it makes us kind. Bahá’u’lláh teaches that the door of knowing the Ancient Being is closed to every mind, and that God in His mercy raises up in each age a pure and stainless Soul as mirror of His attributes, channel of His grace, and the Way joining this world to the realms above. No one reaches the sun, yet anyone can turn to a mirror filled with its light; to know these luminous Beings is to know God. John’s account of the Word made flesh, declaring the unseen God, speaks to the same longing in its own language [1]. The road leads on to the Holy Spirit that joins mirror to Sun, the Primal Will from which the Word proceeds, and the presence of God met in the presence of His Manifestation.
subjects.arc: Begin with love expressed as kindness, then explore revelation, the limits of conception, the mirror of divine attributes, spiritual education, and the directions of prayer.

order.why: Explore the Book of Certitude’s account of inaccessible Essence and accessible revelation.
shortened: The door of the knowledge of the Ancient of Days being thus closed in the face of all beings, the Source of infinite grace, according to His saying: "His grace hath transcended all things; My grace hath encompassed them all" hath caused those luminous Gems of Holiness to appear out of the realm of the spirit, in the noble form of the human temple, and be made manifest unto all men, that they may impart unto the world the mysteries of the unchangeable Being, and tell of the subtleties of His imperishable Essence. These sanctified Mirrors, these Daysprings of ancient glory are one and all the Exponents on earth of Him Who is the central Orb of the universe, its Essence and ultimate Purpose. From Him proceed their knowledge and power; from Him is derived their sovereignty. The beauty of their countenance is but a reflection of His image, and their revelation a sign of His deathless glory.

order.why: Open with the reported test of spiritual conception through kindness toward people.
State knowledge and presence as the purpose of revelation.
shortened: The purpose of God in creating man hath been, and will ever be, to enable him to know his Creator and to attain His Presence. To this most excellent aim, this supreme objective, all the heavenly Books and the divinely revealed and weighty Scriptures unequivocally bear witness. Whoso hath recognized the Dayspring of Divine guidance and entered His holy court hath drawn nigh unto God and attained His Presence, a Presence which is the real Paradise, and of which the loftiest mansions of heaven are but a symbol.

order.why: Read grace through the channel and the human capacity it awakens.
shortened: These Essences of Detachment, these resplendent Realities are the channels of God's all-pervasive grace. Led by the light of unfailing guidance, and invested with supreme sovereignty, They are commissioned to use the inspiration of Their words, the effusions of Their infallible grace and the sanctifying breeze of Their Revelation for the cleansing of every longing heart and receptive spirit from the dross and dust of earthly cares and limitations. Then, and only then, will the Trust of God, latent in the reality of man, emerge, as resplendent as the rising Orb of Divine Revelation, from behind the veil of concealment, and implant the ensign of its revealed glory upon the summits of men's hearts.

order.why: Read the Manifestations as the way through which mercy reaches humanity.
shortened: O Salman! The door of the knowledge of the Ancient Being hath ever been, and will continue forever to be, closed in the face of men. No man’s understanding shall ever gain access unto His holy court. As a token of His mercy, however, and as a proof of His loving-kindness, He hath manifested unto men the Daystars of His divine guidance, the Symbols of His divine unity, and hath ordained the knowledge of these sanctified Beings to be identical with the knowledge of His own Self. Whoso recognizeth them hath recognized God.
Every one of them is the Way of God that connecteth this world with the realms above, and the Standard of His Truth unto every one in the kingdoms of earth and heaven.

order.why: Make the distinction vivid through sun and mirror.
shortened: Is it possible for man to reach the sun? It is clearly impossible and unattainable. But reaching the mirrors is possible. The wise person does not strive to reach the sun, but rather observes the luminous effulgences of the sun in mirrors and becomes connected to them.

order.why: Consider the comprehensiveness of the perfect mirror.
shortened: Now, all created things tell of this light, partake of its rays and receive their portion thereof, but the full splendour of the perfections, bounties and attributes of the Divinity shines forth from the reality of the Perfect Man, that is, that unique Individual Who is the universal Manifestation of God. For the other beings have each received only a portion of that light, but the universal Manifestation of God is the mirror held before this Sun, and the latter manifests itself therein with all its perfections, attributes, signs and effects.

order.why: Read the chosen Individual as a gathering of perfections.
shortened: But in this age of splendours, this era of God, the pre-eminent Personage, the luminous Orb, the chosen Individual will shine out with such perfections and such power as ultimately to dazzle the minds of every community and group. And since such a Personage is superior to all others in spiritual perfections and heavenly attainments, and is indeed the focal centre of divine blessings and the pivot of the circle of light, He will encompass all others, and there is no doubt whatsoever that He will shine out with such power as to gather every soul into His sheltering shade.

order.why: Consider the focal point through which spiritual light is received.
shortened: As to the Holy Manifestations of God, They are the focal points where the signs, tokens and perfections of that sacred, pre-existent Reality appear in all their splendour.

order.why: Ground the discussion in the purpose expressed in the Most Holy Book.
Read presence through the Manifestation’s own statement.
shortened: Attainment unto the Divine Presence can be realized solely by attaining His presence. Through His potency everything that hath, from time immemorial, been veiled and hidden, is now revealed.

order.why: Explore names such as First, Last, Seen, and Hidden.
shortened: And when He purposed to manifest His beauty in the kingdom of names and to reveal His glory in the realm of attributes, He brought forth His Prophets from the invisible plane to the visible, that His name "the Manifest" might be distinguished from "the Hidden" and His name "the Last" might be discerned from "the First", and that there may be fulfilled the words: "He is the First and the Last; the Seen and the Hidden; and He knoweth all things!" Thus hath He revealed these most excellent names and most exalted words in the Manifestations of His Self and the Mirrors of His Being.

order.why: Consider the relation between recognizing Him and knowing God.
shortened: Whoso hath known Him hath known God, and whoso hath turned away from Him hath turned away from God, the Help in Peril, the Self-Subsisting.

order.why: Read the Bab’s distinction between inaccessible Essence and manifested presence.
Follow the Bab’s account of the Sun of Truth and Primal Will.
shortened: And since the recognition of the Ancient Invisible Essence has been impossible, and God the Exalted has not commanded it for any - since its possibility in the contingent realm is impossible - He has enjoined upon all things, from the beginning that has no beginning to the end that has no end, to know the Sun of Truth which is the Mirror of His Essence and the Primal Will which is the Throne of His Manifestation.

order.why: Keep the Book of Names’ veil and shadow imagery in its own devotional setting.
shortened: Say, He Whom God shall make manifest is indeed the Primal Veil of God. Above this Veil ye can find nothing other than God, while beneath it ye can discern all things emanating from God. He is the Unseen, the Inaccessible, the Most Exalted, the Best Beloved.

Say: The likeness of all things is as a shadow before His primal Will. Do ye not see? Say: Light hath no existence before the sun riseth. Even so, ye existed not before God made manifest the Sun of Truth in your religion.

order.why: Distinguish a temporal sign from the descent of the divine Essence.
shortened: The truth of this matter is that the contingent hath ever been contingent, unable to know its Lord, and the Eternal shall never descend to be known in Its Essence. He hath brought forth, through the outpouring of His power and the sovereignty of His creative Will, a sign in the realities of souls and horizons that they might be guided thereby to His knowledge and know Him through it. It is a temporal sign indicating God, the All-Glorious, insofar as is possible within its essence, though none knoweth Him as befitteth Him save Himself, and none describeth Him save He.

order.why: Read the reported explanation of indwelling through reflection.
Consider the preexistence of the Word.
Explore the junction of the two seas of prophethood and divinity.
shortened: Then know, O thou who walkest in the path of God and gazest upon the beauty of God, that by "the junction of the two seas" is meant the sea of Prophethood and the sea of Divinity - that is, to reach the station wherein one attaineth unto the sea of Lordship which surgeth within itself, and every wave thereof proclaimeth that there is none other God but Him, Who created creation from nothing by His command "Be! and it is," and brought the contingent world into being from naught by His word, and He is the Mighty, the Beloved.

order.why: Read spiritual life through the contrast of Christ and Adam.
shortened: Adam is the cause of man's material life, but the reality of Christ, that is, the Word of God, is the cause of his spiritual life.  It is a life-giving spirit, meaning that all the imperfections imposed by the material life of man are, through the instruction and guidance of that Essence of detachment, transmuted into human perfections.  Therefore, Christ was a life-giving spirit and the cause of the spiritual life of all mankind.

order.why: Distinguish independent Prophets from those who receive their light.
shortened: The independent Prophets are each the Author of a divine religion and the Founder of a new Dispensation.

These Prophets acquire the outpouring grace of the divine Reality without an intermediary. Their radiance is an essential radiance, like that of the sun which is luminous in and of itself and whose luminosity is an essential requirement rather than being acquired from another star: they are like the sun and not the moon. These Daysprings of the morn of Divine Unity are the fountainheads of divine grace and the mirrors of the Essence of Reality.

order.why: Consider the reported account of the Holy Spirit as rays.
shortened: So we can say there must be a Mediator between God and Man, and this is none other than the Holy Spirit, which brings the created earth into relation with the 'Unthinkable One', the Divine Reality.

The Divine Reality may be likened to the sun and the Holy Spirit to the rays of the sun. As the rays of the sun bring the light and warmth of the sun to the earth, giving life to all created beings, so do the 'Manifestations' bring the power of the Holy Spirit from the Divine Sun of Reality to give light and life to the souls of men.

order.why: Read the related description of the Holy Spirit as intermediary.
shortened: As there must be an intermediary to transmit to earth the life-giving power of the sun, so there must be an intermediary to bring God to man, and this is found through the ever-present efficacy of the Holy Spirit.

order.why: Place spiritual intermediaries within the public address’s argument.
shortened: As the essence of Divinity transcends the comprehension of man, therefore God brings forth certain Manifestations of the divine Reality upon Whom He bestows heavenly effulgences in order that They may be intermediaries between humanity and Himself.

order.why: Consider Christ through an account of universal mercy.
Explore the relation of intermediary, image, and mirror.
Bring light, veils, and the heart into the mystical journey.
shortened: 47 Indeed, the references that have been made to the degrees of mystic knowledge pertain to the knowledge of the effulgences of that Sun of Truth as it becometh reflected in various mirrors. And the effulgence of that light is present within the hearts, yet it is hidden beneath the veils of selfish desires and earthly attachments, even as a candle within a lantern of iron, and only when the cover is lifted doth the light of the candle shine out.

order.why: Consider the orientation toward a known Center.
Read the distinction between a theoretical direct way and its realization.
shortened: O thou maid-servant of God! No one hath any way to the Reality of Deity except through the Instrumentality of the Manifestation. To suppose so is a theory and not a fact.

order.why: Keep the reported limits of mental conceptions in view.
Ask what naming can and cannot disclose of the Essence.
shortened: Therefore, all these names and attributes belong to the Manifestation of God.

In order to understand an object, we must become greater than that object and then give to it a name and define it with clear definitions; now when we come to God and its essence we can never know anything about It. We come in touch with that divine ineffable "Somewhat" only when we stand before the Manifestation.

order.why: Read the reported appeal to a tangible reality rather than a private figment.
shortened: He then went on to demonstrate that such worship was the worship of a figment of the imagination and had no reality; we must worship God through something tangible and real to us, hence the role of the Manifestations.

order.why: Consider the circle of knowledge and the spiritual world.
shortened: Where the ever-widening circle of man's knowledge meets the spiritual world a Manifestation of God is sent to mirror forth His splendour.

order.why: Read the reported response to the claim that a Manifestation is unnecessary.
shortened: Furthermore, many say, 'We have no need of divine Manifestations; we ourselves have direct communication with God.' They do not know that the divine Manifestations are the bright rays of the Sun of Truth and a means of educating the realities of man.

order.why: Consider the reported appeal to John’s Gospel within its own argument.
Keep the reported comparison of religions attributed to the speaker.
Explains the intermediary between God and humanity through the founders of religions.
Read the tension between expecting a Prophet and recognizing one.
shortened: Man's guardian is God, but to assist man, God provides for him a Prophet. All nations and people are anxiously waiting an appearance of a Prophet. They wish Him to come, but when He does so, they do not recognize Him.

order.why: Consider the image of a messenger sent to every city.
Read Books and Messengers as gifts of grace.
Hear the claim that earlier Prophets are connected through Him.
shortened: He is indeed the One through Whom every Prophet was raised up, every Messenger was sent forth, and every irrevocable decree was revealed.

order.why: Keep the Bab’s orientation toward Him Whom God shall manifest.
Read recognition across successive manifestations.
shortened: In every Manifestation shall Our Self be made known unto all things to the extent that they turn to know Us; these are they who truly know, who verily know God, their Lord; these are the Names of 'Ali by which they infer the knowledge of God, their Lord. Then shall I make My creation to know Me by the Manifestation of Mine own Self: whoso knoweth Him is the first of My creation.

order.why: Consider beholding the Manifestation as meeting the Lord.
Read representation through the image of a mouthpiece.
shortened: The Person of the Manifestation hath ever been the representative and mouthpiece of God. He, in truth, is the Dayspring of God’s most excellent Titles, and the Dawning-Place of His exalted Attributes.

order.why: Consider the relation of the Manifestation’s commands and words to God.
shortened: For the recognition of His Self is the recognition of God, His commandments are God's commandments, His utterance is God's utterance, and His word is the Word of God. Whoso turneth away from Him hath turned away from God, and whoso turneth unto Him hath turned unto God. No one's knowledge and deeds are accepted save through His love and good-pleasure, His command and will.

order.why: Attend to the distinctive significance of His movements.
shortened: Were one to observe with illumined vision, all the movements of the Truth - whether standing or sitting, walking or resting, speaking or silent - would be seen as distinguished and sanctified above the deeds of all who are in the heavens and the earth.

order.why: Read knowledge of God through recognition of Him.
shortened: But for Him none would have attained to the knowledge of God or comprehended the loftiness of His unity and the sublimity of His singleness.

order.why: Consider the Mission’s proof in His own Person.
shortened: He Who is everlastingly hidden from the eyes of men can never be known except through His Manifestation, and His Manifestation can adduce no greater proof of the truth of His Mission than the proof of His own Person.

order.why: Read the images of balance and path.
shortened: He, verily, is God's balance among His servants and His path amongst His creation.

order.why: Keep the path and balance beside the statement about the seal of prophethood.
Consider good pleasure while preserving the distinction from the unseen Essence.
Hear the servant’s role as a summoner.
shortened: And He has sent unto you one of His servants with an authority that was manifest in truth, to call you unto Him and draw you nigh unto the court of exalted glory.

order.why: Read the Messengers as lamps.
Connect those lamps with knowledge and response.
Consider guidance through knowledge and wisdom.
Read the summons to life through the servant’s address.
shortened: Say: O people! This is the servant of God Who summoneth you unto God and guideth you to the paths of guidance, and imparteth unto you mysteries that were forbidden to the peoples of the world, and causeth the breezes of life to waft upon you, and sendeth forth the fragrant breaths of the All-Merciful from the City which God hath sanctified beyond all knowledge and which hath been veiled from the eyes of the mystics.

order.why: Return to the reported image of one center and a pure mirror.
Hear the reported account of channels.
Consider the need for spiritual connection.
Read the reported focal point in prayer.
Consider prayer’s direction and the risk of worshipping a mental creation.
shortened: Abdul-Baha said:

"If we wish to pray we must have some object upon which to concentrate. If we turn to God we must direct our hearts to a certain center. If man worships God otherwise than through his Manifestation he must first form a conception of God and that conception is created by his own mind.

order.why: Retain the reported instruction to turn toward Baha’u’llah.
Read prayer through the reflection of being.
shortened: When the path was cut off and proof failed and the guide lost the way on this path, Thou didst create a luminous being and a merciful reality and made it the sign of perfection, comprehensive of all attributes, and the word of majesty, gathering together the established realities in the highest degrees. It wholly reflects the identity of Thy essence and the conditions of Thy being.

order.why: Hear the Bab’s prayer through the Manifestation.
Consider the limits of understanding and the turn toward the Daysprings.
Read the Daysprings within a prayer for the message to spread.
shortened: Having barred the way that leadeth unto Thee, Thou hast, by virtue of Thine authority and through the potency of Thy will, called into being Them Who are the Manifestations of Thy Self, and hast entrusted Them with Thy message unto Thy people, and caused Them to become the Daysprings of Thine inspiration, the Exponents of Thy Revelation, the Treasuries of Thy Knowledge and the Repositories of Thy Faith, that all men may, through Them, turn their faces towards Thee, and may draw nigh unto the kingdom of Thy Revelation and the heaven of Thy grace.

order.why: Hear the prayer’s countenance, Temple, and horizon imagery.
Consider assistance through the Prophets.
Read the turn toward acceptance.
Hear the cord of loving-kindness as an image of attachment.
shortened: Whoso holdeth fast unto Him hath surely held fast unto the cord of My loving-kindness and clung to the hem of My generosity.

order.why: Read praise through the Way, the Book, and knowledge.
shortened: Praise be to God Who sent down the Proof to His servants, made manifest to them the Way, and caused them to know the Dawning-Place of His Cause, the Rising-Point of His verses, the Source of His laws, and the Recipient of His knowledge - He Who stood before all faces and spoke that which draweth the servants nigh unto the court of His glory and the horizon of His Cause.

order.why: Keep the reference to Ali as a link between earth and heaven.
shortened: O Hasan! Bear thou witness within thyself that He is God, the Mighty, the Wise, and that He Whom He hath sent under the name of 'Ali is His proof unto His creatures, His evidence unto His creation, and His link between the heavens and the earth.

order.why: Retain the cited tradition concerning God, Muhammad, and Ali in its own setting.
Hear the Bab’s distinctive self-description.
shortened: When He created contingent beings by His Command - and the contingent is unable to reach or ascend unto Him, and the Truth, glorified be He, is too glorious and great to be known by anyone, for knowledge is contingent upon conjunction, which is an attribute of contingency, while He, the Truth, is far more exalted and mighty than this - divine wisdom necessitated that He describe Himself to contingent beings, though His description is His origination from nothing.

order.why: Keep fear and reward within the Bab’s address.
shortened: Those who fear their Lord regarding the Gate, secretly and openly in truth -- verily We have ordained for them by God's leave in the Hereafter forgiveness in truth and a great reward.

order.why: Close the linked readings with mysteries expressed through trees and rivers.
Read the supplied guidance permitting prayer directly to God or to the Manifestation.
Retain the related distinction between Baha’u’llah as a door and God.
Consider the supplied account of reflection without embodiment.
Read the supplied statement of one eternal Spirit.
Place the supplied Johannine excerpt beside the full comparative passage.
Consider spiritual experience and the inner meanings of heaven and hell.
Retain the supplied account of influence beyond death with its omission visible.
Read the supplied distinction among God, Will, and creation.
shortened: The prophets, however, maintained the existence of three worlds: the world of God, the world of the Will or the Word, and the world of created things. The Prophets, therefore, maintained that a knowledge of God is impossible.... There is, therefore, only one way to God and that is through the realization of His Manifestation or Prophet in that age. Christ called the world of the Prophets the Word in the verse of "the Word became flesh" while 'Abdu'l-Baha calls it the Will. Anyhow it is only through these that we can know God. These manifest the divine attributes and therefore by knowing them we can know God.

order.why: End with Mirza Abu’l-Fadl’s distinction between spiritual guidance and historical or scientific description.
shortened: It is clear that the prophets and Manifestations of the Cause of God were sent to guide the nations, to improve their characters, and to bring the people nearer to their Source and ultimate Goal. They were not sent as historians, astronomers, philosophers, or natural scientists. Their position in the world of creation is like that of the heart in the body: it has a universal position with a general effect.

questions: What does the mirror image help explain about knowing God, and where might its limits lie?
How does the reported connection between love of God and kindness toward people test an idea of spiritual knowledge?
What relationships among the Manifestation, the Holy Spirit, and the Primal Will emerge across the different texts?
How does John 1:14–18 approach the disclosure of the unseen God, and what distinctive language does each tradition use?
How might permission to pray directly to God illuminate the role attributed to the Manifestations?
What changes when recognition is understood as a relationship that educates character and conduct?

references.label: 1 · John 1:14–18 · The Word, grace, and the unseen God
references.note: Read the King James Version’s account of the Word dwelling among human beings, grace received, and the Son declaring the unseen God. Compare the questions it addresses with those raised by the mirror and channel images. Attend to the distinctive Christian language of the Word made flesh and to the distinction these Baha’i readings draw between divine Essence and its reflection.

subjects.displayTitle: Signs of God in all things: learning to read creation
subjects.introduction: Bahá’u’lláh says that a single leaf holds volumes of knowledge and wisdom, and the Báb warns that even an ant carries within it the most excellent names of God, so that no creature may be belittled. To live by that teaching is to walk through a world that is always an open book, where every atom is a door and the sunlight on a stone, a tree, a mirror is one light received according to different capacities. The vision carries a discipline inside it: a sign is not the Essence, and the mirror that gives back the sun does not become the sun. Qur’an 2:164 reads day and night, the rain and the living creatures as signs for people who understand [1]. The road leads on into the interconnectedness of all things, into the development of capacity that decides how much light a being can hold, and into the human soul as the one mirror able to reflect every name at once, which is why such attentiveness ends in humility and love for people.
subjects.arc: Begin with wonder in a leaf and respect for a small creature, then explore the distinction between signs and Essence, differences of capacity, and the ethical consequences of attention.

order.why: Explore the Book of Certitude’s light in all things and the seeker’s changed perception.
shortened: Nay, whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth is a direct evidence of the revelation within it of the attributes and names of God, inasmuch as within every atom are enshrined the signs that bear eloquent testimony to the revelation of that most great Light. Methinks, but for the potency of that revelation, no being could ever exist. How resplendent the luminaries of knowledge that shine in an atom, and how vast the oceans of wisdom that surge within a drop!

Then will the manifold favors and outpouring grace of the holy and everlasting Spirit confer such new life upon the seeker that he will find himself endowed with a new eye, a new ear, a new heart, and a new mind. He will contemplate the manifest signs of the universe, and will penetrate the hidden mysteries of the soul. Gazing with the eye of God, he will perceive within every atom a door that leadeth him to the stations of absolute certitude. He will discover in all things the mysteries of divine Revelation and the evidences of an everlasting manifestation.

order.why: Open with the many volumes of meaning within one leaf.
Give wonder an ethical direction through the counsel not to belittle a creature.
shortened: Say: All things within their limits manifest the signs of the One in His presence. Can ye not see? Even if ye were to look upon an ant, ye would find within it all these most excellent names in its creation. Therefore, belittle not any of God's creatures, but look unto Him Who created all things by His command.

order.why: Read the ear’s hidden melody and the training disclosed by every atom.
Approach the world as a book to be read.
Consider the universe as an unfolding educational text.
Clarify the distinction between signs and the divine Self.
shortened: Every created being however revealeth His signs which are but emanations from Him and not His Own Self. All these signs are reflected and can be seen in the book of existence, and the scrolls that depict the shape and pattern of the universe are indeed a most great book.
Consider the rays of the sun whose light hath encompassed the world. The rays emanate from the sun and reveal its nature, but are not the sun itself.

order.why: Read unity in revealed signs while preserving the distinction between creation and Truth.
shortened: Unity is to behold the revelation of Truth in all signs, not to consider creation as Truth.

God grant that, with a penetrating vision, thou mayest perceive, in all things, the sign of the revelation of Him Who is the Ancient King, and recognize how exalted and sanctified from the whole creation is that most holy and sacred Being. This, in truth, is the very root and essence of belief in the unity and singleness of God.

order.why: Consider fish, water, and the differing colors of mirrors.
shortened: In another connection He saith: "O Sun-like Mirrors! Look ye upon the Sun of Truth. Ye, verily, depend upon it, were ye to perceive it. Ye are all as fishes, moving in the waters of the sea, veiling yourselves therefrom, and yet asking what it is on which ye depend." And likewise, He saith: "I complain unto thee, O Mirror of My generosity, against all the other Mirrors. All look upon Me through their own colors."

order.why: Join the sign within things to polishing the human mirror.
shortened: Through the pure bounty of His grace and the sublime excellence of His mercy, He hath deposited within all things that are seen and known the sign of His knowledge, that no thing might be deprived of recognizing His presence according to its capacity and station. And this sign is the mirror of His beauty in creation, and the more this most exalted, most wondrous, and most impregnable mirror is polished through striving and endeavor, the more shall the manifestations of His names and attributes and the evidences of His knowledge and signs be impressed and reflected therein, to such degree that every thing may witness in its place and every thing may know its limit and measure, and may hear from all things that there is no God but Him and that 'Ali-Qabli-Nabil is the Manifestation of all names and the Dawning-Place of all attributes, that all were created by His will and all act by His command.

It is clear and evident that when the veils that conceal the realities of the manifestations of the Names and Attributes of God, nay of all created things visible or invisible, have been rent asunder, nothing except the Sign of God will remain—a sign which He, Himself, hath placed within these realities.

order.why: Read the Manifestations as mirrors without imagining the sun embodied.
shortened: All the perfections, bounties and splendours of the one true God are plainly visible in the realities of His Holy Manifestations, even as the light of the sun is fully reflected with all its perfections and bounties in a clear and spotless mirror. And if it be said that the mirrors are the manifestations of the sun and the dawning-places of the daystar of the world, this is not meant to imply that the sun has descended from the heights of its sanctity or has become embodied in the mirror, or that that limitless Reality has been confined to this visible plane. God forbid! This is the belief of the anthropomorphists.

order.why: Consider the related mirror explanation in the discussion of the Trinity.
shortened: The Perfect Man, however, is even as a clear mirror in which the Sun of Truth is revealed and manifested in the fullness of its attributes and perfections. Thus the reality of Christ was a bright and polished mirror of the greatest purity and clarity. The Sun of Truth, the Essence of the Divinity, appeared in that mirror and manifested its light and heat therein, yet it did not descend from the heights of holiness and the heaven of sanctity to reside within it. No, it continues to abide in its loftiness and sublimity, but has been revealed and manifested in the mirror in all its beauty and perfection.

order.why: Read knowledge through perfections rather than comprehension of Essence.
shortened: It is clear, then, that the essential reality of God is revealed in His perfections; and the sun, with its perfections, reflected in a mirror, is a visible thing, an entity clearly expressing the bounty of God.

order.why: Hear the public address’s account of names, signs, and traces.
shortened: But the question may be asked: How shall we know God? We know Him by His attributes. We know Him by His signs. We know Him by His names.

If we wish to come in touch with the reality of Divinity, we do so by recognizing its phenomena, its attributes and traces, which are widespread in the universe. All things in the world of phenomena are expressive of that one reality. Its lights are shining, its heat is manifest, its power is expressive, and its education, or training, resplendent everywhere.

order.why: Explore how universal testimony coexists with the limits of knowledge.
shortened: How all-encompassing are the wonders of His boundless grace! Behold how they have pervaded the whole of creation. Such is their virtue that not a single atom in the entire universe can be found which doth not declare the evidences of His might, which doth not glorify His holy Name, or is not expressive of the effulgent light of His unity.

How can I claim to have known Thee, when the entire creation is bewildered by Thy mystery, and how can I confess not to have known Thee, when, lo, the whole universe proclaimeth Thy Presence and testifieth to Thy truth?

order.why: Retain the Bab’s distinction between signs and the inaccessible Essence.
Read the Bab’s account of divine self-sufficiency as proof.
Consider the Five Modes’ account of bounty throughout things.
Read attraction to handiwork beside transcendence of Essence.
shortened: It is undisputed, however, that the influence of Thine attraction hath everlastingly been inherent in the realities of Thy handiwork, although that which beseemeth the hallowed court of Thy providence is exalted beyond the attainment of the entire creation.

order.why: Hear the likeness of unity in the atom.
Keep the discussion of veils and Adam in its own interpretive setting.
Read universal radiance within the mystical journey.
shortened: To him "all songs are from that sovereign King" and every melody from Him. He sitteth on the throne of "Say, all things are of God" and reclineth upon the seat of "There is no power nor strength but in God alone." He looketh upon all things with the eye of Unity, and seeth the effulgent rays of the Sun of Truth shining from the dayspring of the Divine Essence upon all created things alike, and beholdeth the lights of Unity reflected upon all creation.

order.why: Consider the human capacity to disclose many attributes.
shortened: Upon the inmost reality of each and every created thing He hath shed the light of one of His names, and made it a recipient of the glory of one of His attributes. Upon the reality of man, however, He hath focused the radiance of all of His names and attributes, and made it a mirror of His own Self. Alone of all created things man hath been singled out for so great a favor, so enduring a bounty.

order.why: Read the related contrast between particular things and human comprehensiveness.
shortened: Now, the world of existence, indeed every created thing, proclaims but one of the names of God, but the reality of man is an all-encompassing and universal reality which is the seat of the revelation of all the divine perfections. That is, a sign of each one of the names, attributes and perfections that we ascribe to God exists in man.

order.why: Explore degrees within the names and realities.
shortened: Praise be to God Who hath ever caused His Names and Attributes to penetrate the degrees of existence; Who hath made the effects of those Names and Attributes to shine resplendent and their signs to be firmly established in both the hidden and manifest worlds. By them He hath made the Sanctified Realities, they who are the Recipients of the grace of God and the Bearers of glad-tidings, to be the sole Revealers of His Being, and hath caused them to move in the firmament of perfection in descending and ascending arcs. He hath ordained them to be the origin and cause of existence in the world of creation and the source of gradated realities in the degrees of being.

order.why: Consider the reported sun and transparency analogy for capacity.
Read borrowed light in relation to receptivity.
Consider the reported contrast between fertile and barren ground.
shortened: The divine bounty is universal. The outpourings of the All-Merciful descend successively upon all created things, yet each being receiveth according to its capacity and ability.

The clouds, for example, pour down rain equally from the sky. In one place it falleth upon fertile soil where seeds are sown, and in another place upon barren salt land. Though the rain hath fallen equally upon both, from one there springeth forth a harvest, while from the other only useless thorns and meaningless weeds.

order.why: Hear the reported account of endless variety among images.
shortened: Throughout the universe the divine power is effulgent in endless images and pictures.
In the endless variety of its reflections the divine Will is manifested.

order.why: Read bounties across the kingdoms of existence.
shortened: But although the reality of Divinity is sanctified beyond the comprehension of its creatures, it has bestowed its bounties upon all kingdoms of the phenomenal world, and evidences of spiritual manifestation are witnessed throughout the realms of contingent existence.

order.why: Keep the leaf and atom discussion within its reported natural philosophy.
shortened: The vegetable plane or kingdom, for instance, has its infinite variety of types and material structures of plant life -- each distinct and different within itself, no two exactly alike in composition and detail -- for there are no repetitions in nature, and the augmentative virtue cannot be confined to any given image or shape. Each leaf has its own particular identity -- so to speak, its own individuality as a leaf. Therefore, each atom of the innumerable elemental atoms, during its ceaseless motion through the kingdoms of existence as a constituent of organic composition, not only becomes imbued with the powers and virtues of the kingdoms it traverses but also reflects the attributes and qualities of the forms and organisms of those kingdoms.

order.why: Consider souls and the world as signs of a universal Reality.
shortened: When we examine the world and the souls of men, the perspicuous signs of the perfections of the Divinity appear clear and manifest, for the realities of all things attest to the existence of a universal Reality. The reality of the Divinity is even as the sun, which from the heights of its sanctity shines upon every land, and of whose radiance every land and every soul receives a share.

order.why: Read the claim that no atom lacks a sign.
shortened: Nothing moves except through Thy all-conquering power over all things, and not an atom exists but that it reveals the manifest signs of Thy oneness throughout all regions.

order.why: Hear the concealed sign within every mirror.
Describes signs of divine power and wisdom deposited in every atom.
Pause over the names entrusted to things.
Read rock, clay, and tree as bearers of glory.
shortened: O servant of Baha! The reality of all things proclaims with eloquent tongue "Glory be to my Lord, the Most Glorious!" and the essence of rock and clay and tree cries out "Glory be to my Lord, the Most Exalted!"

order.why: Consider leaf, stone, and clod as witnesses.
shortened: Every leaf and stone and clod hath testified to the appearance of God and His sovereignty, yet the people deny and perceive not.

order.why: Hear the reported account of phenomena speaking.
Read existence as a scroll of praise.
Consider the Bab’s account of praise through being.
Read signs of love throughout things.
Keep universal testimony within the address to Christians.
Read the kingdom through its signs.
shortened: Thou seest, then, O Thou Who art the Beloved of the world and the Revealer of the Most Great Name, how He hath come down with the kingdom of His signs, and in a manner that hath caused the atoms of the earth to testify that the whole world hath been filled with these signs.

order.why: Consider the divine attributes in things alongside transcendence.
shortened: The true believer in divine unity is one who sees all things as manifestations of God's primal sign, and beholds in all things the expressions of His names and attributes, while seeing that sign as sanctified above all things and sovereign over all things - how much more so the Truth Himself, exalted is He above being associated with His creation or known through aught else.

order.why: Explore each thing as a door and path.
shortened: Every single thing among all things is a door leading to His knowledge, a sign of His sovereignty, a revelation of His names, a testimony to His majesty and power, and a path unto His straight way.

order.why: Read manifestation throughout things together with being above them.
Retain the reported Five Treasures passage and its sea imagery.
shortened: The Fifth Treasure: When the Ancient Beauty opened the gate of joy and glad-tidings to the face of the people of creation, He spoke this supreme word: "I have come to this world to extract essences. If there exists an atom of essence in a stone behind the seven seas, I will not cease until I have extracted that essence from it."

order.why: Consider sovereignty through the smallest signs.
Hear the concise proclamation through all things.
Read the summons voiced by atoms.
shortened: Today all atoms proclaim "The Sovereign hath come!" and all the Concourse on High give glad tidings to the people of creation that "Thy Lord hath come, and on that day sovereignty belongeth unto God."

order.why: Consider the vibration of creation in the Tablet of Carmel.
shortened: Sanctified be the Lord of all mankind, at the mention of Whose name all the atoms of the earth have been made to vibrate, and the Tongue of Grandeur hath been moved to disclose that which had been wrapt in His knowledge and lay concealed within the treasury of His might.

order.why: Read heaven, earth, and wind through spiritual meanings.
Explore movement and song without awareness of Mover and Singer.
shortened: In this luminous century, if you observe carefully, the atoms of creation are in motion and movement, and the realities of all things are in vibration and gladness, yet they are unaware of the Mover and Creator. A wondrous melody reaches the ear of the soul and conscience of all, yet they know not the Singer.

order.why: Bring the inquiry back to the absence or presence of attentive ears and eyes.
Hear the reported image of the universe as a theatre.
Read the reported account of mirrors of glory.
shortened: God is the source of all things that are made, and all things that are, are mirrors reflecting His Glory.

order.why: Retain the reported fragment concerning the sun and Christ with its boundary visible.
Consider the public address’s image of all things submerged in bounty.
Read all existence through joy and divine generosity.
Join a repository of wisdom with gratitude.
shortened: I perceive that Thou hast made all things to be the manifestations of Thy behest, and the revelations of Thy handiwork, and the repositories of Thy knowledge, and the treasuries of Thy wisdom.
I yield Thee such thanks as can make every created thing to be a book that shall speak of Thee, and a scroll that shall unfold Thy praise.

order.why: Connect the names and capacities with unity, Covenant, and service.
Retain the particular exhortation to steadfast helpers.
shortened: I beseech Thee by the Word through which, when it was raised up in the world, all things spoke and the earth and heaven were stirred, to make me steadfast among Thy servants in service to Thy loved ones who have traversed the lands to propagate Thy Cause and to kindle hearts with the fire of Thy divine Tree.

order.why: Read rejoicing and thought through the personal address.
Hear the songs of fruits and leaves.
shortened: All things - fruits, trees, leaves and flowers - are singing melodies and are occupied with the praise and glorification of God.

order.why: Preserve the interrupted source passage without supplying its missing connection.
Read the prayer for veils to be removed from sight.
shortened: Remove the veil from mine eyes, O my Lord, that I may recognize what Thou hast desired for Thy creatures, and discover, in all the manifestations of Thy handiwork, the revelations of Thine almighty power.

order.why: Consider the prayer’s every-tree imagery beside scriptural memories.
shortened: This is the hour when Thou hast unlocked the doors of Thy bounty before the faces of Thy creatures, and opened wide the portals of Thy tender mercy unto all the dwellers of Thine earth. I beseech Thee, by all them whose blood was shed in Thy path, who, in their yearning over Thee, rid themselves from all attachment to any of Thy creatures, and who were so carried away by the sweet savors of Thine inspiration that every single member of their bodies intoned Thy praise and vibrated to Thy remembrance, not to withhold from us the things Thou hast irrevocably ordained in this Revelation -- a Revelation the potency of which hath caused every tree to cry out what the Burning Bush had aforetime proclaimed unto Moses, Who conversed with Thee, a Revelation that hath enabled every least pebble to resound again with Thy praise, as the stones glorified Thee in the days of Muhammad, Thy Friend.

order.why: Hear the prayer’s evidences of the divine countenance in creation.
shortened: Hold Thou me with the hands of Thy power, and grant that I may be so carried away by the sweet melodies of the Dove of Thy oneness, that I will cease to regard in all creation any face except Thy face, O Thou the Goal of my desire, and will recognize in the visible world naught else save the evidences of Thy might, O Thou Who art the God of mercy!

order.why: Read handiwork through grace in prayer.
shortened: My God, my God! Every seeing one beareth witness to Thy greatness and power, and every hearing one to Thy might and strength and authority. Thou art He Who, O God of Names and Creator of heaven, hath deposited within all things among created things the traces of Thy handiwork and the manifestations of Thy grace and loving-kindness.

order.why: Consider the illumination of all things.
Hear the prayer’s fire of love through every atom.
shortened: All the atoms of the earth have celebrated Thy praise, and all created things have been set ablaze with the drops sprinkled by the ocean of Thy love, and yet the people still seek to quench Thy fire.

order.why: Read the ocean within a drop beside the love of everyone.
shortened: I implore Thee by Thy Name that hath caused to surge within every drop the oceans of Thy loving-kindness and mercy, and to shine within every atom the luminaries of Thy bountiful blessings and favors, -- I implore Thee to adorn every soul with the ornament of Thy love, that none may remain on Thine earth who hath not turned towards Thee, or hath failed to detach himself from all except Thy Self.

order.why: Close the linked readings by connecting this vision with love for people.
shortened: Our spiritual perception our inward sight must be opened, so that we can see the signs and traces of God's Spirit in everything. Everything can speak to us of God - everything can reflect to us the light of the Spirit.
When we look at people, we must look at them for the spirit that is in them; we must see them in their relation to God - they are His creatures and belong to Him.

order.why: Retain the supplied alternative wording concerning divine self-evidence.
Read the hidden divine presence in the heart through the supplied prayer.
Consider the supplied reflection in myriad forms.
Read bounty as widely bestowed.
Keep Ethel Rosenberg’s reported sun analogy attributed.
Place the supplied Quranic extract beside the complete comparative reading.
Read Nicholas of Cusa’s supplied image of center and circumference in its own philosophical setting.
End with the supplied image of creation rejoicing while retaining the omissions.

questions: How might attention to a leaf or a small creature change habitual ways of valuing the world?
What distinction do the texts draw between a divine sign and the divine Essence?
How does the idea of capacity help readers appreciate variety without reducing every being to the same expression?
What forms of attention and understanding does Qur’an 2:164 invite?
How do the passages connect contemplation of creation with the cultivation of human virtues?
What responsibilities toward people and other living things might follow from seeing them as bearers of signs?

references.label: 1 · Qur’an 2:164 · Signs in the world
references.note: Read Pickthall’s complete translation, alongside the Arabic and parallel translations. Notice how the verse joins natural cycles, living creatures, and useful human activity within its invitation to understanding. Compare this attention to signs with the compilation’s leaf, mirror, and capacity images. The supplied Quranic excerpt retains its own wording and omissions.

subjects.displayTitle: Letters and numbers: symbols, interpretation, and spiritual purpose
subjects.introduction: Within a single point, the Báb teaches, lie hidden worlds of letters, words and phrases, and from the point beneath the letter Bá the whole realm of distinction comes into being. To follow letters and numbers through the Writings is to enter a way of seeing in which the alphabet unfolds into names of God, nine stands as the highest digit and the value of Bahá, and the ringstone and the year nine carry more than arithmetic can hold. The same sign may be read differently in every realm, and the wayfarer is promised a secret in every name. The way has its cautions too. Bahá’u’lláh calls this a day for answering the Call rather than for questions, and the Writings warn that the sciences of numbers neither nourish nor satisfy, that correspondences can be bent to fit a wish, and that a life is better spent quickening one heedless soul. John’s vision of the Alpha and Omega [1] shows how two letters can hold beginning, ending and abiding presence while their scriptural setting disciplines what they may mean. The journey opens onward into the outward and inward meanings of scripture, the many meanings a verse can bear, and the deeper question of how language is woven into the structure of reality.
subjects.arc: Begin with the many meanings of a letter, explore the point, names, and numerical correspondences, then bring elaborate symbolism into conversation with cautions about interpretation and fruitful action.

order.why: Open with the Seven Valleys’ account of meaning changing with the realm of reading.
shortened: 92 The novel thoughts thou hast expressed as to the symbolism contained in the word "sparrow" were considered. Thou appearest to be well grounded in mystic truth. However, in each realm, to every letter a meaning is allotted which pertaineth to that realm. Indeed, the wayfarer findeth a secret in every name and a mystery in every letter.

order.why: Explore the many worlds contained within a limited point.
Read letters branching from and returning to the point.
shortened: Whosoever attaineth unto this station hath attained unto the source and beginning of all knowledge. All infinite letters branch forth from the Ocean of the Primal Point, and unto it do they return and find their end. And whoso knoweth the Point is enriched above the knowledge of aught else, and in the inmost of the inmost essence, whoso knoweth the Point knoweth that whereof the outer letters are composed and that which brancheth forth from them.

order.why: Consider creation through the point beneath the Ba.
Read the sequence from sacred books to the point beneath a letter.
Explains correspondences assigned to letters in abjad symbolism.
Consider the Primal Point through finality and forms.
shortened: The Primal Point, after traversing the realms of the Kingdom, appeared adorned with the seal of finality, and from its composition diverse forms became manifest, culminating in the Most Great Form.

order.why: Explore the Bab’s geometry of point, Alif, and creation.
shortened: And praise be to God Who brought the existences into being through the embellishment of the mystic Alif, self-subsisting, which was originated through the causation of the Point before it and was brought into being through the essence of the aforementioned Will, in its own rank, through it, by it, unto it.

Thus it is neither of primordial eternity nor of ultimate perpetuity, but rather it shineth forth from the Sun of Oneness, gleaming from the glory of the Impenetrable, enduring through the endurance of the Supreme Identity.

order.why: Keep the reported account of point and oneness within its philosophical setting.
shortened: The letters (alphabet) and the numbers (arithmetic) have a mystic correspondence with transcendent reality.

The plurality (27 to 28) of the letters can be traced back to the point (nuqtih), in the case of the numbers, to the one. The point of the world of letters and the one of the world of numbers thus become a universal principle which conditions, penetrates and limits the world of appearances.

order.why: Read the stations of Alif and the comprehensive Jafr.
Consider comprehensive Jafr through the Temple of the Manifestation.
shortened: As for what you mentioned about jafr - the comprehensive jafr in its primal reality is the Temple of the Manifestation. This station is a summary - God willing, after entering the depths of certitude you will become aware of a matter that is more precious in God's sight than all else.

order.why: Keep the requested letters in the Haykal context.
Read Alif, Lam, and Ra through the Qayyum al-Asma’s symbolism.
shortened: God, there is no God but He, hath created the letter Alif for His servant with commanding power. God, there is no God but He, hath ordained the letter Lam for His wisdom according to the decree of the Book. God, there is no God but He, hath made the letter Ra for the expansion of His Cause as He willeth in the Mother Book, decreed in truth around the Fire.

order.why: Follow the relation of Mim, divine Will, and fire.
Read Muhammad’s letters through an account of creation.
Consider the point, eighteen, nineteen, and the Basmalah.
shortened: The one addressed is the Kaf, and He Who addressed it is God, exalted and glorified be He. He revealed Himself unto it through itself at the locus of the Point; wherefore He ascribed unto it the station of Oneness. All this hath been set forth in the ranks of reality -- tenfold in the essential grades, eighteen immutable, and nineteen in motion -- within the sphere of cycles and the pole of the circles of directions.

order.why: Keep Quddus’s interpretation of Quran, Basmalah, Ba, and point attributed.
shortened: Verily all that the Qur'an containeth is encompassed in the Surih of Praise, and all that it containeth is encompassed in the Basmalah, and all that the Basmalah containeth is encompassed in the letter Ba, and all that is in the Ba is encompassed in the Point, and I am that Point beneath the Ba.

order.why: Read the relation of the alphabet and the grammatical verb.
Retain the articulation scheme and its religious judgments as this source’s interpretation.
shortened: Praise be to God Who created the letters according to the repetition of the name of the All-Bountiful from His own Self, and the letter la that the tongues of all created things might proclaim His praise in the letter la without the judgment which the Christians have taken therefrom in the form of the cross, and the Divine Nature resolved the alif of unity in the human nature of the letter of multiplicity which is the lam.

Know thou that God hath created in thee the luminous and dark letters from fourteen points of articulation. The first is a path of truth we hold fast to, and the second is all other letters beside these.

order.why: Hear the alphabet unfold into names and praise.
Read the alphabet through virtues and prayer.
Consider Quranic letters in relation to laws.
Read the luminous Tha and the names associated with fruit.
shortened: We have sent forth in the land of contingent beings a luminous Letter Tha to illumine all who dwell in the kingdom with its light, that they may become victorious helpers of the All-Merciful, and that they may testify within themselves that He is the Truth, there is no God but Him, the Lord, and He is powerful over all things.
Verily I am the letter Mim between Tha and Ra, remembered. Verily I am the letter Ra, I was visible in the letter Jim of the word Thamar (fruit).

order.why: Retain the concealed sequence of Qaf, Fa, and Alif.
shortened: And if thou findest him in his first temple, say: Verily the letter Qaf and Fa with the addition of Alif thereto hath been concealed. If thou art able, bring it forth through a power from Us and a sovereignty from Our presence, and I am, verily, the Mighty, the Beloved.

order.why: Hear the unveiling imagery of Ha and Ba.
shortened: When will the countenance of the letter Ha without garment unveil itself and the face of the letter Ba without veil reveal its mystery? So that the mighty throne may quiver and the ancient seat be filled with delight.

order.why: Keep the reported explanation of abjad values attributed.
Ground the symbolism of nine in the Most Holy Book.
Read nine as the greatest single digit in the decimal system.
Explore the ringstone explanation through Bab, Baha, and Adam.
Retain the related reported calculation and its source omission.
shortened: So number 9 is the highest, and from it all other numbers are made.
For example, the calculation of the number of the word "Bab" is number 5, and Baha is 9. Now, if you multiply 9 by 5 you have 45. Now 45 is the Arabic numerical value of the word Adam:
Aliph equals		 1
Dal equals			 4
Mim equals			40
and the sum of all is	45
As Adam is the Father of humanity and it means the real man, therefore the product of the number of the Bab and Baha is equal to the number of Adam.

order.why: Consider the year nine as a horizon of good.
shortened: His exalted Word states: "In the year Nine ye shall attain unto all good, and in the year Nine ye shall attain unto the presence of God." And addressing His Holiness the Great One (upon Him be all the most glorious glory and the most exalted exaltation), He says - His exalted Word:
This is what We promised thee aforetime when We answered thee.

order.why: Read the related year-nine passage.
Follow the interpretation of Hin and the years sixty-eight and sixty-nine.
shortened: Then he cites the blessed verse from the Furqan which states "This is but a Reminder for all the worlds, and you shall surely know its tidings after a time," meaning that focal point is the Remembrance of God, and what He announces will become manifest and evident in the year after sixty-eight, which corresponds to the numerical value of "time," and after "time" is sixty-nine, meaning it will bear fruit, just as the Exalted One [the Bab] has stated: "Then in the year nine you shall attain all good."

order.why: Retain the parallel interpretation in its separate source.
shortened: Then came this blessed verse: "This is naught but a Reminder to the worlds" - that is, the one asked about is but the Great Remembrance of God, and "ye shall surely know its tidings" means what He will inform and announce "after a time" - that is, after the year sixty-eight corresponding to the numerical value of "Hin" (time), for after year sixty-eight comes year sixty-nine, and this is the year of the manifestation of the Ancient Beauty, as the Most Glorious Beauty, exalted be He, hath said: "Then in the year nine ye shall attain unto all good."

order.why: Read the seventy-seventh Hidden Word and the Greatest Name.
Consider patience and the year nine in relation to the Bayan.
Read the eight letters of the Greatest Name in the Bab’s account.
Keep the designation of the Bab as the Seven Letters.
shortened: There is no God but Him, and verily the Being of the Seven Letters ['Ali-Muhammad] is His servant and His Word. God has chosen for Him names of His Primal Nature equaling the essential numbers of all things, and through them have the heavens and the earth and all that lies between them been filled. Verily, there is no God but Him, the Supreme, the Self-Subsisting.

order.why: Read the correspondence of Joseph and Qayyum together with the priority of deeds.
Consider the detailed letter values in the Dala’il commentary.
shortened: In the first line He inscribed the letters of the abjad, and from its twenty-eight letters, which are the source and return of all things, He derived the name Vahid. In the second line He took the dots marking the ranks of ones, tens, hundreds and thousands, wherefrom the name Mahbub was derived.

Similarly He recorded in each line the equivalents of each abjad letter and derived therefrom a name, until He reached the similar ta's, which represent the ultimate degree of geometry and forms in the material world, from which He derived the name Haqq.

order.why: Read the point, bearers, and Throne within their particular interpretive setting.
shortened: As for what appears in the Visitation Prayer of the Prince of Martyrs (may the souls of those near to God be sacrificed for him), namely "Through thy tribulation the Point left its position and took for itself a station beneath the letter B" - know that the Point's position is at the heading of the Book of Creation, and that the Point is differentiated by the Alif, and the Alif is repeated in numbers, thus manifesting exalted letters and perfect words.

As for the blessed verse "Eight shall bear the throne of thy Lord on that day" - know that the eight bears the nine, and this indicates that the number of the Most Great Name is nine, as it sits upon the eight that bears its throne.

order.why: Retain the Face and the fourteen Innocents as a specific symbolism.
shortened: The learned ones maintain that "Face" refers to the proofs of the Prophet, since the numerical value of "face" is 14, referring to the fourteen holy Innocents (peace be upon them).

order.why: Explore the reversal involving Vav and Alif.
Keep the concise reference to two Vavs.
Read Ha, the Night of Power, and the value of Vav.
shortened: We have adorned the Night of Power with the letter "H" that the people of Baha may attain certitude through this Most Great, Supreme Name. Through it was the Qur'an adorned aforetime, and when combined with "V" the number six appears, if ye be of them that understand.

order.why: Consider Huva, the six days, and the remaining Ha.
Read the limits of comprehension through Waw and Ha.
Retain the related account of six and the manifestations.
Consider Waw through divine decree and its stations.
shortened: And among the things which God hath decreed by confirmation, and which He hath caused to come to pass through bada', is that whereunto I now allude in the obscurities of these intimations, that it may draw thee unto the sacred court of the Throne of the Names and Attributes. It is this: that for the letter waw, the first letter of that verse, there should be appointed a direction abstracted from the six directions.

order.why: Read the contrast of Alif and Waw within the Bab’s symbolic vocabulary.
shortened: Say: The difference between the letter Alif in fire and the letter Waw in light is the numerical value of the Gate. Thus does God transform fire into light for those who were prostrating before God their Lord.

order.why: Keep the seven letters, planets, and stages of creation within their historical cosmology.
shortened: This concerns the science of the letter "Ha" in the reckoning of numbers. Thus was the letter "Waw" established in numerical calculation, and the ordinance of days and their relation to the seven planets - such is God's decree in the science of the Point, as the heart hath truly witnessed, and the heart did not falsify what it saw.

Verily God hath created for the letter Alif the decree of Paradise and its people, then for Ha the decree of Will, then for 'Ayn the decree of Divine Determination and its hosts, then for Ta the decree of Destiny and its like, then for Kaf the decree of Permission and its sister, then for Lam the decree of the Book and its similitude, then for Qaf the decree of the Appointed Time and its form.

order.why: Read the Jafr circle in its Qa’im setting.
shortened: In the school of the People of God it hath been made manifest that the Dispensation is a circle of Revelation [da'iratu'l-zuhur]; and this same circle is, in very truth, four thousand. It is the Jafr of 'Ali -- upon Him be peace -- for it hath been established in the science of the adepts of jafr that the Book of 'Ali -- peace be upon Him -- opened with four thousand and ended with four thousand, a perfect circle. None who obtaineth sight thereof falleth short of beholding, in the very Essence of Manifestation, the arising of the Qa'im -- exalted be He.

order.why: Retain the numerical and alchemical scheme as a historical religious text.
Read the Five Modes’ elaborate correspondences without turning its alchemical claims into established science.
shortened: God hath created through numbers, and the knowledge of everything is in everything, and God hath ever been powerful and mighty over this.

Say: God loves that knowledge, which is the science of numerical values of letters, just as in the letter "Ba" you write the figure two. Say: This is an inaccessible and exalted knowledge - whoever is given it has been given a great bounty.
And I created the letters and made them the keys to all knowledge from Our presence, for We have power over all things.

order.why: Keep the sequence from Alif to Nun and its value in context.
Attribute the numerical claim about death prediction to its source.
Retain the opaque letter and age correspondences without supplying a decoding.
shortened: And verily what ought to be manifested is that which is manifest above all things, and hidden beneath all things, and first before all things, and last on the right of all things, and dominant on the left of all things, according to what is in the traditions concerning the age of thirty. And verily from the first descent of the water of His being until the time He spoke the number of Ta and Kaf, and We have not made thee aware of it, and from an ancient living soul the letter of peace, and it has been fulfilled according to what the pure Family of God have informed after peace, the cycle of fire.

order.why: Read repetitions of disconnected letters in relation to the Most Great Ali.
Consider the human pentagon and the Temple’s letters.
Read the withholding of books and the prayer to inscribe letters within hearts.
shortened: And in the days when neither the Letters are among you and the Point hath been concealed by God's leave, deliver it unto the Gates of Guidance from your Guardian, and give it to none save God, and preserve it with those who are trustworthy among your kindred.

Establish, O my God, all the letters in the hearts of men, their spirits, their souls and their bodies, and transform, O my God, all the letters into those letters which Thou lovest to mention and which Thou permittest to appear before Thee as prostrate servants.

order.why: Hear the prayer’s Ba and circle of life.
shortened: Write the letter Ba in the third circle of my life, for I verily testify to Thy unity after my certitude in Thy glorification and my acknowledgment of Thy praise, that there is no God but Thee.

order.why: Read Ba, Ha, and the Covenant in a devotional address.
Keep numbers within the prayer’s negation and affirmation.
Retain the symbolic duration of negation and affirmation.
Read the negation prayer in its particular polemical setting.
Keep the punitive language attributed to this source.
Retain the prayer concerning unbelievers without generalizing its violent imagery into an instruction.
Read annihilation and negation as this text’s devotional language.
Place affirmation and assistance beside the preceding negation texts.
shortened: Glory be unto Thee, O God my Lord! I beseech Thee by Thy Divinity which transcendeth all things, that Thou assist every soul with Alif who believeth in Him Whom Thou shalt make manifest on the Day of Resurrection, the Essence of Thy greatest proof.

order.why: Keep the reported interpretation of Alif, Lam, and Mim with its omission visible.
shortened: A. B. These letters are symbols predicting future events. If you add these letters, each representing a number, without repeating any one of them, the sum total will be the year of the appearance of his holiness the Bab.
Moreover, every letter indicates a station, for example:
Alif, Lam, Mim.
Alif is a sign indicating the station of Divinity.
Lam is a sign indicating the station of Successorship.
Mim is a sign indicating the station of Prophethood.
Again: Lam is Ali.
Mim is Muhammad.

order.why: Attribute the reported musical etymology rather than presenting it as verified linguistics.
Read the explicit explanation that letters can signify knowledge and virtues.
Consider the reported warning that numerical correspondences can be made to fit.
Read the caution that sciences of numbers may fail to nourish.
shortened: However, today the greatest of all things is to strive that perchance ye may save one who is drowning - that is, to quicken one who is dead through the water of Divine love, or guide one who is heedless unto the abode of wisdom. The sciences of numbers neither nourish nor satisfy.

order.why: Consider the warning that answering such questions can become a hindrance.
Read the contrast between unavailable past principles and fruitful results today.
shortened: The science of jafr had currency in the Qur'anic Dispensation, but its derived principles were unknown, therefore correct results were not obtained. But in this Dispensation all are commanded not to pursue matters that do not yield great results.

order.why: Keep the counsel about Jafr within the call to attend to the present Word.
shortened: When thou didst inquire about divination (jafr), in truth this is not and hath never been the day for questions, even as the Primal Point, Who gave the people glad tidings of the Lord of the Beginning and the End, forbade all from asking questions in this Most Great Revelation.

Today the comprehensive book of divination is that Most Exalted Word which hath flowed and will continue to flow from the Supreme Pen. From it can be derived all that lieth concealed within the tabernacle of God's knowledge.

order.why: Distinguish ordinary numerical knowledge from the spiritual aim.
shortened: The science of numbers is one of the common sciences, but the aim of 'Abdu'l-Baha is, that the Heavenly Knowledge and Divine Wisdom encircle the world of existence.

order.why: Consider education and discovery as a wider horizon of useful knowledge.
Close the linked readings with the counsel to devote time to wise teaching.
shortened: What you have expressed regarding the correspondence of numbers, letters and words was noted, but it would have been better if the time you spent on these matters had been spent on teaching the Cause of God with wisdom and utterance.

order.why: Read Peter Smith’s supplied historical account of the nineteenfold structure.
Keep Juan Cole’s supplied account of Ahsa’i as historical interpretation.
shortened: In Shaykh Ahmad al-Ahsa'i's view, then, a primordial text, the Preserved Tablet or the Leaf, made of letters, influences the unfoldment of human existence.

Each of the primordial letters out of which the world was made corresponds to both a name of God and to a plane of reality. His schema in this regard resembles, but is not identical to, the correspondences put forward by Ibn `Arabi, who also held that the twenty-eight basic letters come together to form all things in the cosmos. (in Juan Cole, "The World as Text: Cosmologies of Shaykh Ahmad al-Ahsa'i", http://www-personal.umich.edu/~jrcole/ahsai2.htm)

order.why: Read Saiedi’s supplied discussion of a world of signs with its initial omission retained.
End with the supplied clarification about nine, the Temple, and tact in explanation.
shortened: Regarding your various questions: We must avoid giving the impression of being all tied up with peculiar religious theories; on the other hand, the 9 sides of the Temple, and the 9-pointed star require an explanation, and he feels the best one is this: Nine is the highest digit, hence symbolizes comprehensiveness, culmination; also, the reason it is used in the Temple's form is because 9 has the exact numerical value of Baha (in the numerology connected with the Arabic alphabet) and Baha, is the name of the Revealer of our Faith, Baha'u'llah.
He does not want the friends to be rigid in these matters, but use their judgement and tact, sometimes one statement is exactly the right for one type of mind and wrong thing another.

questions: How does the possibility of several meanings change the way a reader approaches a letter or number?
What does the image of the point suggest about the relationship between unity and multiplicity?
How do names, shapes, and numerical values function differently across these selections?
How does Revelation 1:8 use the first and last Greek letters, and what does that comparison illuminate without making the traditions identical?
What criteria might distinguish an illuminating symbolic reading from a correspondence made to fit a desired conclusion?
How might the counsel to pursue wisdom and useful service guide the time and attention given to intricate interpretations?

references.note: Read the King James Version’s use of the first and last Greek letters alongside its account of divine beginning, ending, and enduring presence. Compare this alphabetic symbolism with the different roles of point, letter, and name in the compilation. Ask how a symbol opens an inquiry into spiritual meaning while its language and scriptural setting constrain interpretation.
